thought: The 7th Company Commander is a company-level officer, ranking between the squad leaders and the regiment commander. Comparing with others: Ma Baoyu has binoculars (squad leader), Ge Zhenlin has rolled sleeves, Song Xueyi has round face, Hu Delin has askew cap, Hu Fucai has satchel, Political Instructor has glasses and notebook, Regiment Commander has long overcoat and gray temples. The Company Commander needs to visually convey middle-ranking officer status and 'standard military bearing.' The most distinctive and historically accurate feature would be a military saber (dao/短刀) in a leather scabbard at his left hip - a symbol of officer authority that was common for company-level commanders in the Chinese military. None of the other characters carry this type of weapon. Combined with neatly wrapped puttees around his lower legs (showing his by-the-book discipline) and a standard crisp military appearance, he becomes immediately recognizable as the company officer. The saber is the primary visual anchor.
distinctive_features: Military saber in leather scabbard at left hip, neatly wrapped puttees around lower legs, crisp standard military bearing
prompt: Full body portrait of an Eighth Route Army company commander standing in a rigid, disciplined stance, embodying standard military bearing and decisive leadership. The man has a stern, weathered face showing battlefield experience, with a serious and focused demeanor. Most prominently, a military saber (dao) in a brown leather scabbard hangs from his left hip, immediately marking his status as a company-level officer - a distinctive weapon none of the enlisted soldiers carry. His lower legs are wrapped with neatly wound puttees in precise diagonal patterns, demonstrating his by-the-book discipline. He wears a crisp blue-gray Eighth Route Army officer's uniform jacket, standard military cap with red star emblem worn perfectly straight, brown leather belt with holstered pistol on right hip (balancing the saber on left), dark cotton pants with the puttees wrapped from ankle to below knee, and sturdy cloth boots. Centered composition, symmetrical framing, eye-level angle. The subject stands against a single colored burnt umber background with high contrast separation, creating a sharp silhouette. Dramatic chiaroscuro lighting from the front-left, casting strong shadows that emphasize the saber at his hip, the precise wrapping of the puttees, and his stern facial features. Cool to neutral color temperature with low-saturation earth tones - muted slate blues, weathered leather browns, dusty grays. The lighting highlights the polished metal fittings of the saber scabbard and the geometric patterns of the wrapped puttees. Solemn, decisive, and authoritative atmosphere, reflecting the standard military discipline of a company commander in 1941 wartime China. Realistic, thick-painted 2D animation style with bold, visible brushstrokes and strong contrast between light and shadow, emphasizing the harsh dignity and epic nature of historical military command. Deep focus keeping the entire figure sharp from head to toe. Non-distorted portrait lens with natural perspective. The overall mood conveys unwavering discipline, decisive command authority, and adherence to military protocol. Cultural portraiture, historically accurate 1941 Chinese Eighth Route Army company officer appearance and equipment, realistic rendering with painterly texture.
ref_description: Officer with military saber at hip and neatly wrapped puttees
